title: Gluten-Free Honey Vanilla Cupcakes
shortDescription: Soft gluten-free honey vanilla cupcakes with 25 minutes prep and 18 minutes bake time, topped with honey buttercream.
description: These gluten-free honey vanilla cupcakes use a mild floral honey instead of a lot of sugar. The crumb stays soft and tender, thanks to a gluten-free flour blend and a splash of buttermilk.
ingredients: 1 3/4 cups gluten-free 1:1 baking flour blend (with xanthan gum)
1/3 cup mild floral honey (clover or orange blossom)
1/2 cup unsalted butter, softened, for frosting
3 tbsp mild floral honey, for frosting
1 tsp pure vanilla extract, for frosting
1 to 2 tbsp heavy cream, as needed
instructions: Preheat oven to 350°F. Line a 12-cup muffin pan with paper liners.
Whisk the gluten-free flour blend, baking powder, baking soda, and salt in a bowl.
Beat 1/2 cup butter, 1/3 cup honey, and sugar together for 2 minutes until fluffy.
Add the eggs one at a time, beating well after each. Mix in vanilla.
Add the dry mix in three parts, alternating with buttermilk. Mix just until smooth.
Divide the batter evenly among the liners, filling each about two thirds full.
Bake for 16 to 18 minutes, until a toothpick comes out clean. Cool in the pan 5 minutes, then move to a rack to cool fully.
For the frosting, beat 1/2 cup butter until pale and smooth, about 2 minutes.
Add powdered sugar, 3 tablespoons honey, and vanilla. Beat on low, then high, until fluffy.
Add cream, one teaspoon at a time, until the frosting is soft enough to pipe.
Pipe or spread the frosting on fully cooled cupcakes. Serve right away or store in the fridge.
tips: Use a gluten-free flour blend that already has xanthan gum, or the crumb may turn crumbly.
Room temperature eggs and buttermilk blend in smoother and give a more even crumb.
Do not overbake. Gluten-free cupcakes dry out fast once the toothpick comes out clean.
Warm the honey slightly before measuring so it pours easily and mixes in fast.

faq.question: Can I use a different honey for these cupcakes?
faq.answer: Yes, but stick with a mild floral honey like clover or orange blossom. Darker honeys like buckwheat will make the flavor much stronger and less delicate.

faq.question: Why are my gluten-free cupcakes dense instead of tender?
faq.answer: This usually means the flour blend lacked xanthan gum or the batter was overmixed. Mix just until the flour disappears, then stop.

faq.question: Can I make these dairy free too?
faq.answer: Swap the butter for a plant based butter stick and use a dairy free buttermilk substitute, like plant milk with a teaspoon of lemon juice. The honey flavor still comes through clearly.

faq.question: How far ahead can I bake these cupcakes?
faq.answer: Bake the cupcakes up to two days ahead and store unfrosted in an airtight container at room temperature. Frost them the day you plan to serve them for the best texture.

conclusion: These honey vanilla cupcakes prove gluten-free baking can still be soft and light. Keep the honey mild and the mixing gentle, and the crumb will stay tender every time.
